newsitem.title: NEPAL: Strike brings Nepal capital to virtual halt.
newsitem.headline: Strike brings Nepal capital to virtual halt.

text.p: A general strike called by Nepali communists protesting against a water-sharing treaty with India brought commercial life in the Himalayan kingdom's capital to a virtual halt on Friday, witnesses said.
Schools and most shops in central Kathmandu were closed and taxis, auto rickshaws and all public transport shut down except for a few state-owned buses, they said.

The National Democratic Front Nepal (NDFN), an alliance between two communist factions, opposes a proposed treaty between India and Nepal over the sharing of water from the Mahakali river on the kingdom's western border with India.
Nepal's parliament began debate on the treaty this week.
The accord aims to resolve a five-year-old dispute over the sharing of benefits from the Tanakpur dam, built by India in 1991 on the Mahakali river.
The treaty spells out the terms of a new multi-billion dollar dam on the river to generate electricity and supply irrigation water.
Leftwing opposition parties complain that the treaty discriminates against Nepal, which is much smaller than its populous and sprawling southern neighbour.
"A new treaty based on the principle of equality should be negotiated," an NDFN spokesman said.
